claims.statement: Polish rules allow one or several renewable generators to share connection infrastructure and explicitly require source owners to create their own cooperation and cost-sharing model; the founder can control a deal by securing an exclusive pairing mandate or option over a project company with underused connection capacity, then standardizing technical matching and multi-owner agreements with energy counsel.

The Polish regulator reports rising grid-connection refusals and, for 2024 cable-pooling activity, only 12 completed shared connections, 49 signed agreements, 62 issued connection conditions, and 47 refusals from 130 applications; a refused development or chronically underused paid-for connection is a measurable loss of development spend, land option time, and stranded grid capacity.

Renewable developers pay regulated or commercially negotiated connection fees and must negotiate individual cooperation where sources share an interface; developers with a refused project and owners of wind or solar connections with complementary unused profiles are identifiable payers using development, grid-connection, land, and project-acquisition budgets when conditions are refused, expire, or remain underused.

contrary_evidence: The regulator's first-year data show 47 refusals among 130 cable-pooling applications, evidence that matching alone does not overcome technical or procedural constraints.
Current Polish cable pooling is limited to renewable installations, and extending it to independent storage has remained a proposed or desired change rather than a safe assumption for the base model.

economics.acquisition_route: Build a public and partner-sourced map of 50 connection situations in Wielkopolska, use the family installer and land or EPC partners to obtain five owner interviews, and secure one exclusive no-upfront pairing mandate before paying for detailed grid and legal diligence.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Closing 10-20 mid-size pairings annually at an assumed 150000-500000 PLN success fee or small project equity position could create cash flow, while retained royalties or stakes and a proprietary connection graph compound into a regional development platform.
economics.founder_time: Approximately 15-25 founder hours per week during active diligence and negotiations; grid studies, legal drafting, and project development are delegated to specialists.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Preliminary 50-70% gross margin on successful mandates after engineering, legal, and sourcing costs, but long failed deal cycles can make portfolio-level margins much lower.
economics.payback: A developer pays only on issued connection conditions, signed pooling agreement, financing, or project transfer; fee should remain a small share of rescued development value versus a fully stranded project.
economics.pricing: Assumed 25000-75000 PLN refundable diligence retainer credited against a 150000-500000 PLN milestone fee, or a negotiated 1-5% project equity or revenue interest where cash is constrained.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Each transaction is episodic, but owners with multiple sites repeat mandates and retained monitoring or revenue interests persist through the project life.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A verified graph of connection conditions, actual hourly utilization, land and project counterparties, refusal reasons, compatible generation profiles, and contract outcomes.
fingerprint.customer: Polish solar and wind developers, owners of underused grid connections, land option holders, and investors with refused renewable projects.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Renewable EPCs, land agents, energy lawyers, family-installer relationships, project-finance advisers, and owners of complementary generation profiles feed bilateral mandates.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: An exclusive connection-capacity pairing and transaction service that identifies complementary projects, structures cooperation, and coordinates grid diligence; revenue is milestone success fee, option spread, or retained project interest.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: A developer or connection owner pays from development and acquisition budget when a refused or underused project gains usable shared conditions, closes a pooling agreement, or transfers to an investor.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: One renewable project lacks grid access while another holds a legally usable connection whose hourly generation profile leaves monetizable capacity idle.

founder_fit: The family renewable-installation company provides unusually direct access to Polish EPCs, developers, and real connection bottlenecks.
Hourly-profile matching and project ranking use the founder's data-science and finance skills.
Exclusive mandates and outsourced engineering keep capital below project-development levels, though negotiation intensity may test the founder's social-energy preference.
risks: Connection rights or project-company interests may be non-transferable, encumbered, or impossible to option without operator consent.
Deals are slow, legally complex, and relationship-driven, potentially conflicting with part-time execution.
Large developers can use internal portfolios to pair projects and may capture the best connections before a broker sees them.

structure.control_point: Exclusive pairing mandates or project-company options over underused connection situations, bound to technical and legal diligence.
structure.critical_dependency: A complementary project must be legally admissible and technically accepted at the existing connection before the underlying rights or land options expire.

thesis: Poland's grid bottleneck has made connection conditions more valuable than another project-development dashboard. Cable pooling creates a new transaction boundary between stranded projects and underused live connections; a broker that controls exclusive mandates, hourly-profile matching, and repeatable multi-owner agreements can earn success fees and selectively retain project upside while building a proprietary capacity graph.
title: Cable-Pooling Connection Options Broker
uncertainties: Can an exclusive mandate be secured without effectively purchasing or financing a project company?
Which refusal reasons are genuinely remediable through cable pooling rather than network reinforcement?
Will pending storage expansion become law, and can the base RES-only model work without it?
